source_ref: Pilch I, Kurasz Z, Turska-Kawa A (2021) Experiencing fear during the pandemic: validation of the fear of COVID-19 scale in Polish. PeerJ 9:e11263, Table 1; doi:10.7717/peerj.11263 (Europe PMC PMC8083179 fullTextXML). Response data: Pilch I, Wardawy P, Probierz E (2021) PLOS ONE 16(10):e0258606, S1 Database .sav.
note: Item codes ARE the source .sav column names (data/pilch_2021_coping_covid.py melts Fear1..Fear7 with var_name='item'; no rename, no positional assignment), but the S1 Database .sav (sha256 01b58168dc17806ee5615333e93a8416d47d811496c376f822a9476c2707baf6) labels those seven variables 'Fear1'..'Fear7' and carries no value labels for them, so this is NOT data_labels -- the .sav holds no wording at all. The response paper (Pilch, Wardawy & Probierz 2021, PLOS ONE 16(10):e0258606) names the instrument as 'the Polish version of the Fear of COVID-19 scale (FCV-19S)' and quotes only one item as an example; it cites its ref [22] for that Polish version. That reference -- Pilch I, Kurasz Z, Turska-Kawa A (2021) PeerJ 9:e11263, CC BY 4.0, same first author -- prints all seven items in Table 1 in the administered Polish, numbered 1-7, each with the original English in parentheses. Those numbered rows are what ships: Polish in item_text, the paper's own parenthesised English (which is Ahorsu et al.'s original FCV-19S wording) in item_text_translated, both transcribed character-for-character from the Europe PMC fullTextXML of PMC8083179 (sha256 c65768ee13e83f79cc93d63b30a7f0adf6119001a4740de284f06a124604e81e), including the source's curly apostrophe in 'I’m' and its absence of terminal full stops. ANCHORS: both papers state the scale only as '(one-strongly disagree, five-strongly agree)' in English prose. The administered Polish anchors are published nowhere in the deposit or either paper, so option_text is left blank for all five levels and the two English endpoint labels ship in option_text_translated; resp 2-4 are unlabelled in the source and are left blank rather than padded with their own numbers. No instructions text is published in either paper, so instructions/section_prompt are blank. MAPPING: verified in verify_pilch_2021_fear_covid19.R -- the PeerJ paper's Sample 1 (N=383) is effectively this same respondent pool (N=387 complete cases here), and all 35 published statistics (per-item mean, SD, corrected item-total r, male mean, female mean) reproduce under the identity mapping with total absolute deviation 0.2740 across 35 numbers; the best of the other 5039 permutations scores 0.5169. RIGHTS: the FCV-19S originators' own article (Ahorsu et al. 2020, Int J Ment Health Addict 20:1537-1545) is CC BY 4.0 and the Polish version's publication (PeerJ 9:e11263) is CC BY 4.0; no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause was located from either rights holder. Not in instrument_rights_register.csv. Same verdict reached for odachi_2022_fear_covid19 in batch_121.
public_note: The seven items ship in the administered Polish with the FCV-19S's original English alongside; the response anchors do not -- neither source publishes the Polish labels, so only the English endpoint labels (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree) are recorded, and the three middle points are left blank.

source_ref: Data/table: Pilch I, Wardawy P, Probierz E (2021) The predictors of adaptive and maladaptive coping behavior during the COVID-19 pandemic in Poland. PLOS ONE 16(10):e0258606, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0258606 (CC BY 4.0); S1 Database, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0258606.s002 (.sav, SPSS 26, 397x61, fetched 2026-09-10). ITEM WORDING (Polish, administered): the published Polish IPIP-BFM-20 form, 'Kwestionariusz IPIP-BFM-20' by Ewa Topolewska, Ewa Skimina, Wlodzimierz Strus, Jan Cieciuch, Tomasz Rowinski, downloaded from the Polish IPIP project's own site www.ipip.uksw.edu.pl (test.php?id=31 -> public_modules/downloadFile.php?fname=Kwestionariusz IPIP-BFM-20.pdf&fpath=1fd6f9081f.pdf), sha256 cb777f82b10d0f5afd22f4b4006a12621fb693fe9a175251027664c7ca052977, fetched 2026-09-10; the form's own footer reads 'Creative Commons Uznanie autorstwa CC BY, 2013' (www.liberilibri.pl). ENGLISH item wording: the IPIP 50-item Big-Five Factor Markers form at https://ipip.ori.org/new_ipip-50-item-scale.htm, same item numbers. Item-set corroboration: Topolewska E, Skimina E, Strus W, Cieciuch J, Rowinski T (2014) Krotki kwestionariusz do pomiaru Wielkiej Piatki IPIP-BFM-20, Roczniki Psychologiczne 17(2):385-402, https://ojs.tnkul.pl/index.php/rpsych/article/download/513/535/ (p. 378: the 20 selected IPIP-BFM-50 items are 1,16,31,46 extraversion; 2,17,22,37 agreeableness; 8,23,28,43 conscientiousness; 9,14,19,39 emotional stability; 5,10,30,50 intellect) and its Table 2, which prints all 50 Polish items starred for selection. IRW processing script: data/pilch_2021_coping_covid.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/pilch_2021_personality_ipip20/.
note: PASS with caveats. (1) STEP 3b / INSTRUMENT: live data is 20 items IPIP1..IPIP20, resp 1-5, n=397 per item, which matches the paper's Measures section exactly ('the International Personality Item Pool-Big Five Markers-20 questionnaire (IPIP-BFM-20), the short Polish version of the IPIP-BFM-50 ... 20 items ... five-point scale (1-very inaccurate, 5-very accurate)'). Table name and dictionary Description are correct. The three sibling tables from the same .sav are different instruments (BEH*/Avoidance*/Wishful* coping, Vulnerab*..Costs* protection motivation, Fear1-7 FCV-19S) and were not touched. (2) SOURCE LEVEL: the study's own .sav is level 1 for the CODES but carries NO item text - all 20 IPIP variable labels are the bare column names ('IPIP1'..'IPIP20') and the file's only value labels are on Gender, Edu, Empl, Marital, Risk1, Risk2. The paper does not reproduce the items either. Wording therefore comes from the published instrument (text_source=canonical_instrument), specifically the adapters' own CC BY form, which numbers its items 1..20 in the administered order. (3) MAPPING: data/pilch_2021_coping_covid.py melts the .sav columns unrenamed (SCALES['pilch_2021_personality_ipip20'] = [f'IPIP{i}' for i in range(1,21)]), so the IRW code IS the source column name - no positional step. What is inferred is that source column IPIPn is form item n. That is recorded as paper_order and checked against the data: see verification_pilch_2021_personality_ipip20.csv and verify_pilch_2021_personality_ipip20.R. Summary: the form's E,A,C,ES,I cycle with alternating keying predicts the subscale structure, and 4 of 5 composites reproduce the paper's Table 2 M to 0.01 and 5 of 5 its SD to 0.01, all five alphas land within 0.033 of the published values, and 9 of 10 published intercorrelations reproduce to 0.006. Rival orderings fail badly (see verification evidence). The residual is that a swap within any of the ten trait-by-polarity pairs is undetectable, so status is PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. (4) A PAPER SLIP WORTH RECORDING, not a data problem: Table 2 gives 'Neuroticism' M = 2.82 SD = 0.86, but the neuroticism-keyed composite computed from the live items is M = 3.19 SD = 0.85, and 2.82 = 6 - 3.19 (the emotional-stability mean). Every correlation Table 2 reports for that variable carries the NEUROTICISM sign and reproduces here (E -0.300 vs -0.30, C -0.189 vs -0.19, A 0.024 vs 0.02, age -0.185 vs -0.18); only r(N,Intellect) disagrees in sign (published +0.12, observed -0.116). Read as two reporting slips in one Table 2 row. (5) LANGUAGE: administered in Polish (Polish general-population adults). item_text/instructions/option_text hold the Polish form verbatim; the _translated columns hold English. The English of the ITEM statements is IPIP's own English for the same numbered items (ipip.ori.org 50-item form) - a parallel original, not a translation of the Polish string. The English of the INSTRUCTIONS and the five response anchors was written by IRW, because the Polish adaptation's instructions and anchors ('calkowicie nietrafnie mnie opisuje' etc.) are the adapters' own text with no published English counterpart; IPIP's English anchors ('Very Inaccurate'..'Very Accurate') are a different, terser wording and were deliberately not substituted. Hence translation_source=mixed, and the IRW-written half is disclosed in public_note. (6) DEVIATION / instructions: the instructions shipped are the paper form's, transcribed verbatim including 'Swoja odpowiedz zaznacz wstawiajac X w odpowiednim okienku' (mark your answer with an X in the box). Pilch et al. ran an online survey, so respondents did not tick boxes on paper; the sentence is kept rather than edited, and the mismatch is disclosed in public_note. (7) RIGHTS: ships. The wording was copied from the Polish IPIP-BFM-20 form hosted by the adaptation's own authors at www.ipip.uksw.edu.pl, whose footer states 'Creative Commons Uznanie autorstwa CC BY, 2013' - an affirmative open grant with no fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term (sha256 cb777f82b10d0f5afd22f4b4006a12621fb693fe9a175251027664c7ca052977). Upstream, the originator is IPIP, whose own site states: 'The items and scales are in the public domain, which means that one can copy, edit, translate, or use them for any purpose without asking permission and without paying a fee' (ipip.ori.org), which expressly covers the translation. NOT relied on: the Topolewska et al. (2014) Roczniki Psychologiczne article, which is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 - it was read only to confirm WHICH 20 IPIP-BFM-50 items were selected (a fact, not wording) and to corroborate the item set; no item string was taken from it. No IPIP row exists in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv; a 'ship' row for IPIP-BFM-20 is owed but the register is shared, so it is left to the orchestrator. (8) COVERAGE: all 20 items use all five resp levels (smallest cell IPIP5 resp=1, n=5), so every item has an option row for every level its own respondents used, and every item has exactly 397 rows - no row-count anomaly. (9) RETRY TEST: not applicable - this table passed and nothing is blocked.
public_note: Item text is the published Polish IPIP-BFM-20 form (Topolewska, Skimina, Strus, Cieciuch & Rowinski, 2014, CC BY), not wording printed by this study - the study's data file labels its 20 columns only 'IPIP1'..'IPIP20'. Two things a reader should know about the English columns: the English item statements are IPIP's own wording for the same numbered items (ipip.ori.org), a parallel original rather than a translation of the Polish; and the English of the instructions and of the five response anchors was written by IRW, because the Polish adaptation's own instructions and anchors have no published English version. The instructions are also transcribed from the paper-and-pencil form and tell the respondent to mark an X in a box, whereas Pilch et al. administered the questionnaire online. Finally, the assignment of each wording to its code rests on the form's own item numbering: the data confirms the five-trait cycle and every item's keying direction (4 of 5 subscale means and 5 of 5 SDs reproduce the paper's Table 2 to 0.01, all five alphas to within 0.033), but it cannot distinguish the two same-trait, same-direction items in each pair, so a swap within a pair such as IPIP1/IPIP11 would be invisible.
